prose.text: - **The live round** is the block's `round` and `live` entries, fired by `gate.py run --live-legs --entry N`, one   drive at a time (step 10). The wrap never re-runs it; it re-verifies from `evidence/`. - **Non-priming probe:** `conductor preconditions --for real-model-interpretation` precedes every drive. It fires   no canary. There is no `boot` before any drive: it would prime the incident the drive's own canary dedupes   against (verification-harness.md 2026-08-19 (a)). - **Operator entries before the round** are fired once, by hand, in block order, their results recorded in the   ledger. The five pre-leg checks run in a shell that sourced the operator's capture env file; no other entry   does. `pulse-app` is launched between them and the round (step 9); the agent starts it and stops it, on the   overseer's go. - **No build entry:** the two Pulse binaries are the fifth series', held by digest in the third entry. - **Each `live` entry ends by printing two stamps** from the frozen self-obs stream. The next invocation deletes   that file, so the entry reads it itself. - **Smoke:** `status` is mint-then-read on `d3`'s `run_id`. - **The attempt ledger has no producing entry:** the agent authors it from the entries' recorded results and from   Pulse's own log. The harvest's `pre_registered` reads its digest line and the host-path probe sweeps it. - **Night rule:** only the three `live` entries are GPU runs. Every other entry runs at any hour. - **Host paths:** the Pulse binary probe runs inside `target/release` with bare file names; the model digest   entry prints the digest alone; the two handle entries print a fixed line. - **Controls owed at implement** (red before green, one-shot): step 12's `measured` table, and one wrong pin   digest shown red by `each_2026_10_07_capture_run_capture_matches_its_pinned_digest` before the real one lands.   Their readings go to the report. - **The operator pass** (hygiene, the pre-CI commit, the guarded push, the CI read) is the operator's. The agent   performs it only on the operator's explicit word, and records it as made on that word.
